name: Dawera-Daweloor
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.source_named: Chlenova, Svetlana. 2002. Daweloor, A Southwest Moluccan Language. Malaisko-indoneziiskie issledovanija 15:145-175 (phonological sketch; not online)
earlier_scan.note: Chlenova 2002 sketch is sole phonological source; Wikipedia phonology section from it has no stress statement

sources.citation: Steinhauer, Hein. 2009. The sounds of Southeast Babar. In K. Alexander Adelaar & Andrew Pawley (eds.), Austronesian historical linguistics and culture history: A festschrift for Robert Blust, 91-105. Canberra: Pacific Linguistics 601.
sources.note: About a DIFFERENT Babar language (Southeast Babar, ISO vbb), not Dawera-Daweloor. p. 96: 'Stress does not seem to be phonemic at the word level. Often the same word occurs with different stress in comparable environments. Below I refrain with some exceptions from indicating stress.' Recorded here only as the nearest-neighbour statement; it cannot be attributed to ddw.

sources.citation: Grimes, Charles E. & Owen Edwards. 2026. The Austronesian languages of eastern Indonesia and Timor-Leste: Unravelling their prehistory and classification. Berlin: Language Science Press (948 pp.). Babar section 4.6.5, pp. 223-236.
sources.note: Historical-phonology treatment only; no stress statement for Dawera-Daweloor. Names Taber 1993 and Chlenova 2002/2012 as the only data sources for the language (p. 224) and quotes Taber's stress-marked form <ˈmɛtmel> 'black' (p. 224 fn 29). The only stress remark is generic: 'While penultimate stress is the normal rule for Wallacean languages, words with penultimate schwa can have stress on other syllables' (p. 115, Bima-Lembata schwa discussion, not about Babar).

sources.citation: Wikipedia contributors. 'Dawera-Daweloor language'. English Wikipedia, raw wikitext retrieved 2026-09-17. Phonology section sourced to Chlenova 2002.
sources.note: Consonant (m n p t k d s h l r w j) and vowel (i u e a o) tables only; nothing on stress or accent.

sources.note: Mentions Dawera-Daweloor only for medial geminates in Taber's (1993) 193-word survey list; states that 'reasonably good descriptive data is available only for Kisar and Luang'. Nothing on stress.
